QW.use: Used to ask about a person.
ex: Who is the president of Spain?
¿Quién va a venir a la fiesta?
Who is coming to the party?

QW.use: Used to ask for information or about something.
QW.tip: With a noun, most Latin Americans say qué: ¿Qué libro prefieres?
ex: What are you going to do today?

QW.use: Used to ask about the time or moment.
Used to ask about the location.
Used to ask for the reason or cause.

ex: Which of these books is better?
Which do you prefer, tea or coffee?

QW.use: Used to ask about possession or ownership.
Used to ask about the way, manner or process.
ex: How do you say this in English?

QQ: Who is the president of Spain?
Which do you prefer, tea or coffee?
How do you say this in English?
What is your date of birth?

when: Habits, routines and facts
Things that are generally true
Opinions and states
TENSES.ex: Yo estudio español todos los días.

when: Actions happening right now
Temporary situations
What somebody is doing at the moment
TENSES.forms: estoy hablando, estás comiendo, está viviendo

when: Past actions with a connection to the present
Life experiences or things you have done
Actions that started in the past and continue now
TENSES.forms: he hablado, has comido, ha vivido
TENSES.note: In Mexico and Colombia people often use the simple past instead. You will hear Ya comí more than Ya he comido.

when: Actions that started in the past and are still happening
To emphasize the duration of an action
Repeated actions up to now
TENSES.forms: he estado hablando, has estado comiendo, ha estado viviendo
TENSES.ex: He estado estudiando toda la tarde.
TENSES.exen: I have been studying all afternoon.

when: Completed actions at a specific time in the past
A series of finished actions
TENSES.exen: I went to the market yesterday.

when: Ongoing actions or situations in the past
Habits, repeated actions or background information
What used to happen
TENSES.ex: Yo vivía en México cuando era niña.
TENSES.exen: I lived in Mexico when I was a child.

when: Past actions with a connection to the present
Life experiences or things you have done
TENSES.forms: he hablado, he comido, he vivido
TENSES.note: Same tense as in the present chart. Latin America leans on the simple past for most of these.

when: An action that happened before another action in the past
To show that something had already happened
TENSES.forms: había hablado, había comido, había vivido
TENSES.ex: Ya había salido cuando me llamaste.
TENSES.exen: I had already left when you called me.

when: Used mainly in formal or literary language
An action that happened immediately before another past action
TENSES.forms: hube hablado, hube comido, hube vivido
TENSES.ex: Apenas hube llegado cuando empezó la reunión.
TENSES.exen: I had barely arrived when the meeting started.
TENSES.note: You will mostly meet this one in books, not in conversation.

when: An action that had been in progress before another action in the past
To emphasize the duration of an action in the past
TENSES.forms: había estado hablando, había estado comiendo, había estado viviendo
TENSES.ex: Había estado estudiando toda la tarde.
TENSES.exen: I had been studying all afternoon.

when: Predictions and promises
Formal plans
Guessing about now: Estará en el trabajo (he must be at work)
TENSES.form: Infinitivo + é, ás, á, emos, án
TENSES.exen: Tomorrow I will talk to the doctor.

when: Polite requests
Advice: yo iría (I would go)
What would happen
TENSES.form: Infinitivo + ía, ías, ía, íamos, ían
TENSES.ex: Me gustaría un café, por favor.
TENSES.exen: I would like a coffee, please.

when: Wishes, doubts and emotions
Recommendations and what is not yet real
After que with a different subject
TENSES.form: Forma yo, sin la o, más la vocal opuesta
TENSES.exen: I want you to speak more slowly.

when: Telling someone to do something
Instructions with patients
Polite commands with usted
TENSES.form: Tú: forma él del presente. Usted y ustedes: subjuntivo.

CONN.sub: Para dar tu punto de vista
Para explicar el motivo o resultado

CNOTE.Eventualmente: Heads up: in everyday Spanish this usually means possibly or occasionally. For eventually, say con el tiempo or al final.
CNOTE.Incluso: Heads up: it usually means even or including. For moreover, use además or asimismo.
CNOTE.En cambio: Heads up: it means whereas or on the other hand. For instead of, say en lugar de.

CQ: I'm tired, that's why I'm going to sleep.
Practico todos los días ___ quiero hablar mejor.
I practice every day because I want to speak better.
Me gusta el café, ___ no me gusta el té.
I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
Primero tomo café, ___ voy al trabajo.
First I have coffee, then I go to work.
There are arepas. In addition, there is mole.
It's cold, however we are going to go out.
___, el español es un idioma bonito.
In my opinion, Spanish is a beautiful language.
___, quiero darles las gracias a todos.
In conclusion, I want to thank everyone.
___ llegó tarde, no vio la película.
Due to the fact that he arrived late, he didn't see the movie.
Me gusta el pan, ___ el pan caliente.
I like bread, above all warm bread.
Mi hermano come mucho; ___, yo como poco.
My brother eats a lot; whereas I eat little.
Hablo tres idiomas, ___, español, inglés y francés.
I speak three languages, in other words, Spanish, English and French.

TOPICS.sub: Two verbs for to be, and when to use each

p: Think DOCTOR: Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time, Origin, Relationship.
Use it for identity, jobs, nationality, time, and where an event takes place.
ex: Son las tres de la tarde.
It is three in the afternoon.
La fiesta es en mi casa.
The party is at my house.

blocks.h: ESTAR: how or where something is
p: Think PLACE: Position, Location, Action, Condition, Emotion.
Use it for location, feelings, temporary states, and the -ing form.
With ser it describes what someone is like. With estar it describes how they are right now.

drill: My mom is in the kitchen.
A condition right now uses estar.
The party is at my house.
An event taking place uses ser.
The patient is very nervous today.
It is three in the afternoon.
Time uses ser, plural for hours after one.
The book is on the table.
Location of an object uses estar.
Ella ___ muy lista, siempre saca buenas notas.
She is very smart, she always gets good grades.
Smart is a characteristic, so ser.
I am ready to go out.
Ready is a state, so estar.

p: Purpose or goal (in order to), recipient, destination, deadline, opinion, and who you work for.
ex: I study to become a nurse.
Necesito la tarea para el viernes.
I need the homework by Friday.

blocks.h: POR: why or how it happened
p: Reason or cause, exchange or price, duration, moving through a place, means of communication, and thanks.
ex: I arrived late because of traffic.
Pagué diez dólares por el libro.
I paid ten dollars for the book.

drill: I study to become a nurse.
This gift is for my mom.
I arrived late because of traffic.
A means of communication uses por.
Who you work for uses para.
I paid ten dollars for the book.
An exchange or price uses por.
I need the homework by Friday.
Moving through a place uses por.

p: The easy future in conversation: voy a, vas a, va a, vamos a, van a, then the verb.
ex: I am going to study tonight.
We are going to eat arepas.

p: Take the whole infinitive and add é, ás, á, emos, án.
Irregular stems: tener tendr-, hacer har-, decir dir-, venir vendr-, saber sabr-, salir saldr-.
It also guesses about now: Estará en el trabajo means he must be at work.
ex: Tomorrow I will talk to the doctor.
I will have time on Friday.

p: Infinitive plus ía, ías, ía, íamos, ían. Same irregular stems as the future.
Use it for polite requests and advice.
ex: Me gustaría un café, por favor.
I would like a coffee, please.

drill: Tomorrow I will talk to the doctor.
El próximo año nosotros ___ a Colombia. (viajar)
Next year we will travel to Colombia.
She will have time on Friday.
Tener has the irregular stem tendr-.
I would like a coffee, please.
A polite wish uses the conditional.
A polite request uses the conditional.
Venir has the irregular stem vendr-.
Decir has the irregular stem dir-.
We will do the report tomorrow.
Hacer has the irregular stem har-.
I am going to study tonight.
Ir a plus infinitive is the going to future.
What would you do in my place?
Would uses the conditional, with the stem har-.

TOPICS.sub: Commands with tú, usted and ustedes

p: Use the él or ella form of the present: habla, come, escribe.
Eight irregular ones: di, haz, ve, ven, pon, sal, sé, ten.
Put no in front and use the subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no vivas.
Both use the subjunctive: hable, hablen. This is the form you use with patients.
ex: Tome este medicamento dos veces al día.
Take this medication twice a day.

p: Pronouns attach to the end of affirmative commands: siéntese, dígame. They go before negative ones: no se siente, no me diga.

drill: Tú affirmative is the él form of the present.
Negative tú commands use the subjunctive.
The pronoun attaches to the end, with an accent.
Ten is one of the eight irregular tú commands.
Ven is one of the eight irregular tú commands.
Negative usted commands use the subjunctive.
Ustedes commands end in en for ar verbs.
Di is one of the eight irregular tú commands.
(Usted) ___ este medicamento dos veces al día. (tomar)
Take this medication twice a day.
Negative tú commands use the subjunctive, and hacer uses hag-.

TOPICS.sub: Wishes, doubts, emotions and what is not yet real

p: Think WEIRDO: Wishes, Emotions, Impersonal expressions, Recommendations, Doubt and denial, Ojalá.
The pattern is main clause + que + subjunctive, usually with two different people.
ex: I want you to speak slowly.
Es importante que tomes el medicamento.
It's important that you take the medication.

p: Start with the yo form of the present, drop the o, and add the opposite vowel.
ar verbs take e, es, e, emos, en. er and ir verbs take a, as, a, amos, an.
hablo becomes hable. como becomes coma. vivo becomes viva.
Irregular: ser sea, estar esté, ir vaya, dar dé, saber sepa. Spelling shifts keep the sound: busco becomes busque, llego becomes llegue, empiezo becomes empiece.
ex: It's necessary that we leave early.

p: Certainty uses the indicative: Creo que viene. Doubt uses the subjunctive: No creo que venga.
Same person doing both things? Use the infinitive: Quiero comer, not Quiero que yo coma.
For a future moment, use cuando plus subjunctive: Cuando llegues, llámame.
ex: Creo que ella está en casa.
I think she is at home.
No creo que ella esté en casa.
I don't think she is at home.
When you arrive at the hospital, call me.

drill: I want you to speak slowly.
Wishes about someone else use the subjunctive.
Estar has an irregular subjunctive: esté.
Es importante que usted ___ el medicamento. (tomar)
It's important that you take the medication.
Ojalá is always followed by the subjunctive.
Dudo que él ___ a la fiesta. (venir)
I doubt he will come to the party.
I recommend that she drink more water.
I want to speak Spanish well.
Same person, so use the infinitive.
No creo que ellos ___ la verdad. (saber)
I don't think they know the truth.
Saber has an irregular subjunctive: sepa.
It's necessary that we leave early.
Salgo is the yo form, so salga, salgamos.
I hope you go with me.
Ir has an irregular subjunctive: vaya.
I think she is at home.
Creo que means certainty, so the indicative.
When you arrive at the hospital, call me.
Cuando about the future uses the subjunctive.

DIFS.sub: Two ways to say to know
words: to know (facts, how to do something)
to know (people, places, things you are familiar with)
Being familiar with someone or somewhere.
ex: I know how to speak Spanish.
I don't know where he lives.
DIFS.tip: If you could say be familiar with, use conocer. If it is a fact or a skill, use saber.
drill: I know how to speak Spanish.
Do you know where the hospital is?
A place you are familiar with, so conocer.

DIFS.sub: Asking for something and asking a question
words: to ask for, to order, to request
ex: I ask where the bathroom is.
DIFS.tip: You pedir a thing. You preguntar a question.
drill: I'm going to ask for the check.
The check is a thing, so pedir.
I want to ask where the bathroom is.
Where it is is a question, so preguntar.
She asks for help when she needs it.
Help is a thing, so pedir.

words: The act of speaking or a language.
DIFS.tip: Hablar is the act of speaking. Decir needs the thing that was said: decir que, decir la verdad.
drill: She tells me she's coming tomorrow.
Something is being said, so decir.
I want to talk with the doctor.

words: Moving away from here, or toward a destination.
Moving toward the speaker or the listener.
ex: Are you coming to my house?
DIFS.tip: In Latin America, Ya voy means I'm coming. Ya vengo often means I'll be right back.
drill: Are you coming with me to the party?
Tomorrow I'm going to the hospital.
Going to a destination, so ir.
A command to come, so ven.
Ya voy is the usual way to say I'm coming.

words: to take, to carry, to wear
Away from here. Also what you wear.
ex: Can you bring me the check?
She is wearing a blue jacket.
DIFS.tip: Bring is traer. Take is llevar. Llevar also means to wear.
drill: Can you bring me the check, please?
Voy a ___ a mi mamá al doctor.
I'm going to take my mom to the doctor.
Take to somewhere else, so llevar.
She is wearing a pink dress.

words: The everyday word in Latin America, for drinking and for taking.
A little more formal or literal. It only means drink.
ex: I drink coffee in the morning.
I'm going to take a taxi.
I drink a lot of water.
DIFS.tip: Tomar does both jobs. Only tomar works for take a bus, take a taxi, take medication.
drill: I'm going to take a taxi.
Take a taxi is always tomar.
Do you want to take the bus or walk?
Take the bus is always tomar.

words: Becomes buen before a masculine noun.
well, fine (describes an action or how you are)
DIFS.tip: Bueno describes a noun. Bien describes a verb or how you feel.
drill: Before a masculine noun, bueno shortens to buen.
Describes a feminine noun, so buena.

words: Goes before an adjective or adverb. Never changes.
Goes with nouns and verbs. Matches the noun.
ex: I have a lot of work.
DIFS.tip: Muy never stands alone and never goes right before a noun.

words: Time as a stretch of duration.
DIFS.tip: Tiempo is time as a stretch, hora is the clock, vez is how many times.
drill: Voy al gimnasio tres ___ por semana.
I go to the gym three times a week.
I don't have time to eat.

DIFS.tip: With a thing, it is wait for. With que and the subjunctive, it is hope.
drill: I hope you get better soon.
Hope that, with que and the subjunctive.
Ella ___ el autobús en la parada.
She waits for the bus at the stop.
Waiting for a thing, no que.

DIFS.sub: Where it is, plans, and staying
words: to be located, to agree to meet, to be left
Where things are, plans, what remains.
DIFS.tip: Quedarse (with se) is you staying. Quedar without it is where things are, or plans.
drill: Where something is located, so quedar.
Hoy ___ en casa porque estoy cansada.
Today I'm staying home because I'm tired.
___ a las cinco frente al hospital.
We agreed to meet at five in front of the hospital.

words: to leave (behind), to let, to quit
to leave, to go out, to come out
ex: Dejo mis llaves en la mesa.
I leave my keys on the table.
Salgo del trabajo a las cinco.
What time does the bus leave?
DIFS.tip: Salir is to leave a place. Dejar is to leave something behind, or to let.
drill: I'm going to leave my keys here.
What time do you leave work?

DIFS.t: tener que vs hay que vs deber
DIFS.sub: Have to, one has to, should
words: one has to, you need to (in general)
A general rule that fits everyone.
DIFS.tip: Tener que is a personal must, hay que is a general rule, deber is advice.
drill: ___ que llenar este formulario. (anyone who comes)
You have to fill out this form.
A general rule, so hay que.
I have to go to the doctor today.
A personal obligation, so tener que.

DIFS.tip: Encantar is for things you adore. Querer is for people you love. Te amo is much stronger and romantic.
drill: I love my grandmother very much.

ex: I arrived late because there was traffic.
I study because I want to learn.
DIFS.tip: A question uses two words with the accent. An answer uses one word without it.
drill: A question, so two words with the accent.
I'm tired because I worked a lot.
Giving a reason, so one word.
Estudio español ___ quiero hablar con mis pacientes.
I study Spanish because I want to talk with my patients.

ex: Me gusta el café y el té también.
I like coffee and tea too.
Ella no habla inglés y él tampoco.
She doesn't speak English and he doesn't either.
DIFS.tip: Positive statement, también. Negative statement, tampoco.
drill: Te dicen: No me gusta el frío. Respondes: Yo ___.
Agreeing with a negative, so tampoco.
Te dicen: Tengo sueño. Respondes: Yo ___.
Agreeing with a positive, so también.
Ella no habla inglés y él ___.
She doesn't speak English and he doesn't either.

DIFS.t: De nada, perdón, disculpe y más
words: Starting a question to a stranger.
For something that matters or for sad news.
excuse me (to pass or to enter)
Walking past someone, entering a room.
ex: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, I'm going to pass.
DIFS.tip: Match the weight: perdón for small slips, lo siento for real sorrow, disculpe to get someone's attention, con permiso to pass.
drill: ___, ¿me puede decir dónde queda el baño?
Excuse me, can you tell me where the bathroom is?
Getting a stranger's attention, so disculpe.
Excuse me, I want to get through.
My grandmother died. I'm so sorry.

DIFS.sub: Now, in a bit, and later
words: right now or in a little while
Very common in Mexico and Colombia. It stretches, so read the situation.
ex: First I study, then I eat.
DIFS.tip: Ahorita is stretchy: it can mean right now or soon. Luego means later or then.
drill: Primero tomo café y ___ voy al trabajo.
First I have coffee and then I go to work.
No puedo hablar ___, estoy en una consulta.
I can't talk right now, I'm in an appointment.
I'll call you later, I'm busy right now.

words: Common in Colombia and much of Latin America.
DIFS.tip: Match the slang to the place: chévere and bacano in Colombia, padre and chido in Mexico.
To ask someone to repeat, use ¿cómo? or ¿perdón? to stay polite. A bare ¿qué? can sound rude.
drill: Una paciente habla bajito. Con respeto dices: ¿___? ¿Puede repetir?
Pardon? I didn't hear you well.
